verses.commentary: Woe to the city of oppressors. After oracles against foreign nations, Jerusalem itself faces judgment. Rebellious (moreah), defiled (nigalah). The city chosen for God's presence has become hostile to God's ways.
Four indictments: obeys no one, accepts no correction, does not trust the Lord, does not draw near to God. The root problem is relational. Not technical violations but broken intimacy.
Officials are roaring lions, rulers are evening wolves leaving nothing for morning. Predatory leadership. Those meant to protect devour. The sheep are eaten by the shepherds.
Prophets are reckless (pochazim, frivolous), treacherous people. Priests profane the sanctuary, do violence to the law (torah). The mediators between God and people have failed from both directions.

Yet the Lord within her is righteous. He does no wrong. Morning by morning he dispenses justice, every dawn without fail. The unrighteous know no shame. Divine faithfulness contrasts with human corruption. God remains just while people abandon justice.
God speaks of destroyed nations, demolished strongholds, deserted streets, empty cities. Historical examples of judgment. Israel has seen what happens to the wicked. Yet they do not learn.
God's hope for Jerusalem: surely you will fear me, accept correction, your dwelling will not be cut off. But they remained eager to act corruptly. Divine expectation met by human intransigence.

Therefore wait for me, declares the Lord. The day God rises to testify. Nations assembled, kingdoms gathered, wrath poured out. Jealous anger consumes. But the waiting leads somewhere beyond judgment.

Then I will purify the lips of the peoples. All will call on the Lord's name, serve shoulder to shoulder. Babel's confusion (Genesis 11) reversed. United worship replaces divided speech. Judgment leads to restoration.
From beyond the rivers of Cush, worshipers and scattered ones will bring offerings. The most distant peoples, the most dispersed, gathered to worship. Geography cannot limit restoration.
On that day Jerusalem will not be ashamed. God removes arrogant boasters. No more haughtiness on the holy hill. Pride purged. Humility remains.
God leaves within Jerusalem the meek and humble. The remnant of Israel trusts in the Lord's name. Character matters more than heritage. Humility qualifies for blessing.

They will do no wrong, speak no lies. No deceitful tongue found among them. They eat, lie down, and no one makes them afraid. Moral transformation produces peaceful existence. Changed hearts create safe community.

Sing, Daughter Zion! Shout aloud, Israel! Rejoice with all your heart, Daughter Jerusalem! The imperatives shift from judgment to celebration. Joy commanded. Worship is appropriate response to salvation.

The Lord has removed your punishment, turned back your enemy. The Lord, King of Israel, is with you. Never again will you fear harm. Punishment ended, enemies defeated, presence restored, fear banished. Comprehensive salvation.
On that day they will say to Jerusalem: Do not fear, Zion. Do not let your hands hang limp. Encouragement for the weary. Fear and helplessness give way to confidence.

The Lord your God is with you, the Mighty Warrior who saves. He will take great delight in you. In his love he will no longer rebuke but rejoice over you with singing. God sings over his people. The warrior rests and celebrates. Divine joy expressed musically. One of Scripture's most tender images.
God removes those who mourn over lost festivals. The burden and reproach of exile ends. What caused grief becomes occasion for joy. Lament transforms to celebration.
At that time God deals with oppressors, rescues the lame, gathers exiles. Praise and honor replace shame in every land. The weak receive strength. The scattered find home. Reputation restored.

At that time I will gather you, bring you home. Honor and praise among all peoples when I restore your fortunes before your eyes, says the Lord. The book ends with homecoming, honor, and witnessed restoration. What began with judgment concludes with grace.
